summary: The change is a one-literal default flip plus a tiny cleanup effect inside the existing SidekickMenu orchestrator, not a new feature. In SidekickMenu.tsx change the destructured default from `searchEnabled = true` to `searchEnabled = false`; the existing render guard `searchEnabled && !effectiveRailCollapsed` then stops mounting the input, its ref stays null, and the existing autofocus effect already no-ops on a null ref, so no new focus code is needed and nothing invisible is focusable. If the prop changes from true to false while a term is still held, the list must not stay filtered by a term the user can no longer see: a second effect dispatches SET_SEARCH_TERM with an empty string when search is off and the term is non-empty. SET_SEARCH_TERM already exists in menuReducer, and the existing pre-search path effect restores the section once the term empties, so no reducer or context change is needed. Enabled search keeps the same lookup, placeholder, icon, autofocus, empty-state, arrow-key and numbered-shortcut code paths untouched, because only the default value and the off-state term reset change. Public surface is unchanged: no export, prop name or type is added, removed or renamed; SidekickMenuProps.searchEnabled stays `boolean | undefined` and only its documented default flips, so UI/index.ts is not touched. This is a behaviour-breaking change for consumers, so package.json goes to 2.0.0, docs/breaking-changes.md gets a v2.0.0 entry naming searchEnabled with the searchEnabled={true} migration, and README.md, docs/api.md, docs/configuration.md, docs/examples.md and docs/features.md stop presenting search as on by default while keeping their prev/next links. Scale: nothing new scales with menu size; with search off the component mounts no input and getFilteredItems returns the array untouched for an empty term, while with search on the existing memoized per-level filtering is unchanged, so a hundred times more items behaves exactly as 1.7.0. Cost: one boolean comparison per render and one guarded effect check, no new state, listeners, timers, storage keys, network calls, dependencies, CSS, exports or files; removing the mounted input when search is off can only shrink or leave equal the built bundle, so the dist size stays within today's budget. Accessibility: with default props the DOM and tab order are exactly the pre-search control set (focus trap still only intercepts Tab at the first/last focusable child and never focuses anything on open), and with searchEnabled the input remains keyboard-reachable and behaves as today.

reuses: The existing `searchEnabled && !effectiveRailCollapsed` render guard in SidekickMenu.tsx (line 505) to unmount the input entirely, so no hidden input exists
The existing null-guarded autofocus effect in SidekickMenu.tsx (lines 329-333), which does nothing when searchInputRef is null
menuReducer's existing SET_SEARCH_TERM action, CLOSE_MENU's existing term/path reset, and the existing pre-search path restore effect
getFilteredItems' existing empty-term fast path in UI/SidekickMenu/utils/search.ts, so search-off filtering is free

The existing search props searchPlaceholder, searchIcon, searchAutoFocus and alwaysShowUnsearchableItems and their propagation to DrilldownMenuList, arrow-key navigation and numbered shortcuts, all unchanged
The existing search input markup, aria-free label text and CSS Module classes, untouched
The existing test setup, helpers (getHamburger, makeItems) and test file layout next to the source
The existing docs prev/next navigation and the breaking-changes entry format (entries oldest-first, v2.0.0 appended last)
adds: One small useEffect in SidekickMenu.tsx that dispatches SET_SEARCH_TERM with "" when searchEnabled is false and searchTerm is non-empty
New tests in SidekickMenu.test.tsx for the hidden default, opt-in rendering, no invisible/focusable input when hidden, and dropping an active term when search is turned off
A v2.0.0 entry in docs/breaking-changes.md naming searchEnabled, stating the new default and showing the searchEnabled={true} migration, plus its table-of-contents item
No new files, no new exports, no new props, no new dependencies, no new components, and no CSS, storage or build-output changes
